newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to detail rules on foreign stocks buying.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to detail rules on foreign stocks buying.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand will later on Tuesday issue a statement detailing rules on how foreigners may transact business in the local stock market, a senior bank official said on Tuesday.
Brokers said on Tuesday that they had been told informally by the central bank to settle transactions undertaken by foreigners in the local bourse only in U.S. dollars.

They had said that the reported central bank move was aimed at preventing foreigners, in need of baht supplies to cover their short positions in the forex market, from raising the Thai unit through sales of stocks in the bourse.

"There will be a statement this afternoon. It will explain all details and procedures for foreigners about investing in the stock market," Thirachai Phuvanatnaranubala, director of the central bank's Financial Institutions Supervision and Development Department told Reuters.
"I want to reassure that foreign investors are still be able to trade shares as usual. The statement will make foreign investors have a better understanding," he said.

The central bank has cut off baht supply from local sources to offshore parties since the middle of May in an attempt to strike back at speculators who led a speculative attack on the baht and held positions against the baht.
The move created an informal two-tier baht market and forced offshore players to scramble for the Thai unit to cover short positions at exorbitant rates, dealers said.
